terms.es: El banco y el cambio de moneda
terms.it: La banca e il cambio valuta

en.title: The bank and changing money
en.summary: Opening an account, withdrawing cash and exchanging currency, with the language of fees and rates.

paragraphs: A bank has its own vocabulary, but most visitors need only a few phrases. In this lesson you will exchange money, ask about fees and discuss opening an account.
A visitor from Spain goes to a bank in London.

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: Good morning. I would like to change some euros into pounds.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: Certainly. How much would you like to change?

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: Two hundred euros. What is the exchange rate today?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: It is eighty-five pence to the euro, so you would receive one hundred and seventy pounds.

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: There is a commission of three pounds. Could I see your passport?

lines.speaker: Visitor
lines.text: Yes, of course. Also, I am staying for six months. Can I open an account?

lines.speaker: Clerk
lines.text: You would need proof of address, but I can give you the information.

paragraphs: **1. Change into and withdraw from.** These verbs take fixed prepositions. See Introduction to Grammar: Verbs and verb phrases.

blocks.html:
PhraseExample
change... intochange euros into pounds
withdraw... fromwithdraw cash from my account
pay... intopay money into an account
transfer... totransfer money to a friend

paragraphs: **2. Would and if show a possible result.** The second conditional with would suggests an unreal or unlikely situation, which is common in polite business talk. See Introduction to Grammar: Moods, command, subjunctive and conditional.

blocks.html:
ConditionResult
If you changed two hundred euros,you would receive 170 pounds.
If you opened an account,you would need proof of address.

items: The exchange rate is the price of one currency in another.
A fee or commission is a charge for a service.
A current account is for daily payments; a savings account earns interest.
Proof of address can be a utility bill or a letter from your landlord.

paragraphs: Many British banks have closed local branches, so most people now use a phone app. Banks usually ask for identity and proof of address when you open an account.
